meta.description: Tests for differentially abundant proteins between conditions with limma/DEqMS empirical-Bayes moderation, proDA/msqrob2/MSstats missingness modeling, and Python Welch+BH alternatives. Frames missing values as left-censored MNAR (model, do not impute), makes variance moderation the load-bearing step at n=3-5, and prefers feature/peptide-level testing. Summarization and normalization mechanics are proteomics/quantification; volcano and MA plots are data-visualization; pathway enrichment is pathway-analysis.
meta.audit_note: Re-audit after pass 3 (e8d2cd4: estimability filter for blocked designs) and pass 4 (0fe7f85: msqrob2 and MSstats feature-level routes, centred-contrast guard). Previous score 82, Limited Release, below the CORE floor of 85. All 9 inputs of the previous audit were re-run as regression tests and 2 new inputs were added, one of which is a controlled test of the causal claim the pass-4 fix rests on. Every number below came from a run made by this auditor on 2026-09-15; the fix log was read but is not evidence.
meta.environment: R 4.4.3 via the candidate's r.sh (limma 3.62.2, DEqMS 1.24.0, proDA 1.20.0, ashr 2.2.63, msqrob2 1.14.1, QFeatures 1.16.0, MsCoreUtils 1.18.0, MSstats 4.14.2); Python 3.12 shared venv (pandas 3.0.5, numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, statsmodels 0.15.0). msqrob2 and QFeatures are now installed, so both routes the Skill recommends are executable for the first time. Nothing was installed and no shared version was changed.
meta.data: ALL SYNTHETIC with planted truth, from audits/bio-proteomics-differential-abundance/data/: a 4v4 MaxQuant set with a batch effect (proteinGroups.txt 1,560 proteins; evidence.txt 1,468 precursors over 299 proteins), a 6-donor paired set, a three-arm set, and the 4v4 truth table. PXD070049 was deliberately NOT used: it carries one replicate per condition under the submitter SDRF, which cannot support a realized-FDR claim.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated results or citations. Every number this audit could check was reproduced within sampling noise: msqrob2 0.0% / 8.0% / 27.9% realized FDR across the three normalizations against the claimed 0.0 / 7.0 / 28.6, MSstats 20.8% as shipped and 21.2% with MBimpute = TRUE (both exact), the invariant 48 up / 32 down true-hit count, posterior df 151.9 peptide-level against 36.4 summarized, and the paired-design 63 calls / 4.8%. One claim in the prose is an unsupported MECHANISM rather than a fabricated number, and is recorded as a P1 below; the numbers attached to it are real.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Scope paragraph explicitly excludes 'single-sample (n=1) comparisons, and diagnosis or treatment decisions for an individual patient', which is the Input 6 boundary.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled fallacy. MNAR framing, trend/robust moderation, the estimability filter for blocked designs, minimum-fold-change testing via treat rather than a double filter, and the honest recalibration of proDA (underpowered for on/off at n=3-5, confirmed here: 0 of 140 on/off proteins called) and of feature-level testing ('not free') are all correct. The refuted mechanism in the centring section does not change any operational instruction: the instruction it supports - do not per-run-median-normalize the peptide table before a feature-level test, and check the centring first - is correct on every configuration tested.

code_usability.detail: All ten fenced blocks were extracted verbatim and executed, including the four added in pass 4 (msqrob2, msqrobAggregate, MSstats, centring guard). All three shipped examples exit 0, and examples/msqrob2_peptide_level.R runs both on real audit data and in its own simulation fallback.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 4: both previously code-free promises now ship - msqrob2 (summarized and msqrobAggregate peptide-level) and MSstats feature-level - alongside limma, treat, DEqMS, proDA, ashr, the Python route and a centring guard; three examples. Correctness 3: every estimator reproduces, but the stated MECHANISM of the centring section is refuted by a controlled test (see Input 10) and its 'significant for hundreds of proteins at once' is an overstatement of the 31 extra false positives measured. Appropriateness 4.

reliability.note: Fault tolerance 4: the pass-3 estimability filter is load-bearing, not cosmetic - without it eBayes fails outright with 'prior.weights contain NA values' on the paired design. Error reporting 4: the centring stop() names the offset, the cause and the Skill to fix it in; seven Common Errors rows each record a real error, two of which this audit hit independently (the ridge refusal verbatim, and readQFeatures needing colData$quantCols). Recoverability 3: stateless.

performance_context.note: Token cost 3: 398 lines (was 284) in one file, ten code blocks, no references/ split. Execution efficiency 4: msqrob2 over 1,468 precursors and MSstats over the same set both return in well under a minute.

agent_usability.note: Learnability 4: each workflow states what its result columns are actually called (adjPval not adj.P.Val, sca.adj.pval, adj.pvalue), which is the class of mistake that silently produces an empty hit list. Consistency 4: the usage-guide drift the previous audit flagged is gone - none of the three contradicting phrases survives in either file. Feedback design 3. Error prevention 3: the MSstats block ships normalization = 'equalizeMedians', which is the setting the centring section two paragraphs later blames for the anticonservative result; one section warns about what the other does.

human_usability.note: Discoverability 3: jargon-dense description, though the vocabulary is the real one. Forgiveness 4 (Category 3 override): hard stops are correct here and each one names the specific failure and the remedy.

security.note: Credential safety 4, input validation 3, data safety 4. No eval/exec of user input, no shell, no network, no credentials anywhere in SKILL.md or the three examples.

inputs.label: NEW: a controlled test of the causal claim the pass-4 centring guard rests on
inputs.note: The claim: the 21.2% realized FDR comes from a global -0.18 log2 offset introduced by per-run median normalization of the peptide table, and realized FDR tracks the offset monotonically. Reproduced: per-run median normalization over all detected peptides gives offset -0.199, 111 calls, 31 FP, 27.9%; complete-case normalization -0.107, 87, 7, 8.0%; none -0.005, 80, 0, 0.0%; and the true-hit count is 48 up / 32 down in every one of them, so the normalization adds only false positives. MSstats reproduced exactly at 20.8% (shipped) and 21.2% (MBimpute = TRUE). REFUTED: injecting a KNOWN uniform offset of -0.20 log2 into every treatment run - exactly the magnitude blamed - gives median log2FC -0.205 and ZERO false positives. The sweep is non-monotone and flat across the range the Skill cares about: 0 FP at -0.20, -0.10, -0.05, +0.05, +0.10 and +0.20; 4 FP at -0.30; 34 at -0.40. Two further measurements isolate what is really happening: per-run median normalization halves the null-protein standard error, from 0.2057 to 0.1159, because it removes genuine within-condition run-to-run loading variation (the per-run shifts span -0.423..+0.246, sd 0.206 within Control alone), while a uniform injected offset leaves the SE at 0.2057 untouched. Neither ingredient alone is enough: centring each run on its OWN condition's median reproduces the SE shrinkage (0.1158) with no offset and yields 1 false positive of 81. The harm needs the offset AND the shrunken SE together, and the SKILL.md prose attributes it entirely to the offset.

The guard behaved correctly in all four: STOPS on the -0.199 and -0.184 tables with the exact shipped message, PASSES on the clean one.

The pass-3 estimability filter is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: with it the 6-donor paired design realizes 4.8% FDR against a 5% cut; without it limma's eBayes does not merely inflate FDR, it fails outright with 'prior.weights contain NA values'.

Its statements about the installed tools are exact where it would be easy to be loose - the ridge refusal message word for word, ridge accepted on three groups, the ~ -1 + condition escape, adjPval vs sca.adj.pval vs adj.pvalue, and readQFeatures needing colData$quantCols. Two of the seven Common Errors rows record errors this audit hit independently before reading them.

The centring guard is protective in every configuration tested: it stops on the -0.199 and -0.184 tables with a message naming the offset, the cause and the Skill to fix it in, and passes on the clean one - even though the mechanism the prose gives for it does not survive a controlled test.

recommendations.title: The centring section's stated mechanism is refuted
recommendations.problem: The Skill says a global between-condition offset of 0.1-0.2 log2 'becomes significant for hundreds of proteins at once' because feature-level standard errors are small. Injecting a uniform -0.20 log2 offset into every treatment run gives 0 false positives, with the null-protein median SE unchanged at 0.2057. Real per-run median normalization at the same -0.199 median offset gives 31 false positives, because it ALSO halves that SE to 0.1159 by removing genuine within-condition run-to-run loading variation. Neither ingredient alone is enough - offset-only gives 0 FP, SE-shrinkage-only (centring each run on its own condition's median) gives 1 of 81. 'Hundreds' is also an overstatement of 31.
recommendations.root_cause: The root-cause analysis varied one family of normalizations, in which the offset and the variance shrinkage move together, and attributed the whole effect to the variable that was easiest to measure.
recommendations.fix: Rewrite the Approach paragraph: per-run median normalization of a peptide table does two things at once - it transfers a detection-composition difference into a between-condition offset, AND it removes real run-to-run loading variance, shrinking the residual the test divides by. The offset is the detectable symptom of both. Keep the guard exactly as it is (it fired correctly on every configuration tested) and add a second cheap check beside it: compare the residual SD before and after normalization, and treat a large drop as the same warning. Drop 'hundreds of proteins at once' for the measured figure.

recommendations.title: The MSstats block ships the normalization the Skill blames
recommendations.problem: The MSstats workflow hardcodes normalization = 'equalizeMedians' and therefore produces a table with a -0.184 offset and a 20.8% realized FDR. The centring guard two paragraphs later then stops the reader. One section of the Skill warns about exactly what another section does.
recommendations.root_cause: The MSstats block was written from the vendor's default call; the centring section was added afterwards without revisiting it.
recommendations.fix: Add a comment on the normalization argument of dataProcess pointing at the centring check, and offer normalization = FALSE with protein-level centring afterwards as the alternative the centring section actually recommends. Show the measured consequence (-0.184, 20.8%) inline so the choice is visible at the point of the call.

recommendations.title: The 0.05 centring threshold has no stated basis
recommendations.problem: The guard stops at |median log2FC| > 0.05. On this data an injected uniform offset of -0.20 is harmless (0 FP) yet would be stopped, and a within-condition centring that halves the SE is harmful in principle yet passes at -0.016. The threshold is calibrated on one 4v4 set and on a symptom whose relation to the harm is not what the prose says.
recommendations.root_cause: The constant was read off the four normalizations tried during the fix pass.
recommendations.fix: State that 0.05 is an empirical trip-wire from one 4v4 label-free set, not a distributional bound; make it a named constant at the top of the block; and say explicitly that passing the check does not certify the normalization, only that this particular symptom is absent.
